answer: A freshly minted alias has no ancestry, so it must first attach itself to real accepted work: 116 new identities mean that many orphan roots to graft by hand rather than print, and each root still needs its own identity record. The ivory graph is validated at intake and the oasis frontier is published, which means the ancestry of every answer is public, and delta anchors the chain at a checkpoint. Honest users pay that once, farms 8 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
